summary.text: Father of the Mysian captains Chromis (`chromis-mysian`) and Ennomus (`ennomus-mysian`) — attested by Apollodorus in the catalogue of Trojan allies, while Homer names the sons but not their sire.

story.text: Homer's Catalogue sets Chromis and Ennomus, the augur who could not ward off black fate, at the head of the Mysian ships — but the poet does not name their father in the muster.

Apollodorus makes Chromius and Ennomus sons of Arsinous among the allies from Mysia. He must be kept distinct from the Arsinous whom Homer names as father of fair-tressed Hecamede, Nestor's cupbearer from Tenedos (*Il.* 11.620–650).
